unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 12-LEVEL: B1.4 THEME 4: CITY & SOCIAL LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will explore the theme ''City Life and Social Life'' by investigating different communities and lifestyles in rural areas and cities, as well as problems related to infrastructure and planning in urban environments and their solutions. They will create a comparative presentation or short documentary highlighting the contrasts between rural and urban lifestyles, focusing on factors like housing, transportation, and community engagement. Additionally, students will identify common infrastructure challenges in cities, such as traffic congestion, inadequate public spaces, or poor waste management, and propose innovative, sustainable solutions. The project should show a deep understanding of how these factors influence social life and contribute to building more inclusive and well-planned communities. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''city life and social life with its components such as different communities and lifestyles in the rural areas and cities; problems related to infrastructure and planning in the city and solutions'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 12 may know what different communities and lifestyles in the rural areas and cities; problems related to infrastructure and planning in the city and solutions mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper secondary school in year 12, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''city life and social life'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''sustainable city, recreational activities, to offer, suburb and so on'' and also some structures such as ''I have been living in this neighbourhood for a long time. We have come across him three times at the concerts. This city will be a slow city in 2030.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''city life and social life with its components such as different communities and lifestyles in the rural areas and cities; problems related to infrastructure and planning in the city and solutions'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about city and rural life, addressing infrastructure challenges and suggesting actionable solutions in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Explore, Analyse, and Suggest The teacher starts with a slideshow or infographic about city and rural life, emphasising infrastructure challenges and potential solutions (e.g., urban traffic, lack of green spaces) while introducing target vocabulary (e.g., cosmopolitan, rapid construction, modernisation), which students record. In groups, students organise the vocabulary into categories (City Life, Rural Life, Problems, Solutions) and choose a picture to describe and evaluate using the new terms (e.g., ''This picture describes a busy urban street with traffic jam and noise pollution''). Next, students write a formal suggestion for addressing an infrastructure issue, explaining the issue, its consequences, and actionable solutions (e.g., ''Traffic jams cause air pollution, but increasing public transportation can reduce it''). Finally, they share their evaluations or suggestions, and the teacher gives supportive feedback on language use and clarity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe city life, rural life, infrastructure problems, and solutions in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Match, Speak, and Learn The teacher shows simple pictures of city life, rural life, and infrastructure problems/solutions (e.g., a farm, a park, or a busy street) and introduces basic vocabulary with clear explanations and gestures (e.g., ''This is a park. People can relax here. Students match the vocabulary (e.g., park, traffic, farm) to the correct picture, then create simple sentences using sentence starters provided by the teacher (e.g., ''In the city, there is _______'', ''In the countryside, people _______''). Example sentences include: ''In the city, there are tall buildings'', or ''In the countryside, people grow vegetables''. The teacher listens and gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
